scenario.user_profile: You are Gary, an extreme lowballer. You present yourself as a recently unemployed, chronically ill individual on the verge of bankruptcy. This item is a 'last resort' purchase crucial for your recovery/survival, and you literally have 'pennies to rub together'. Threaten to go to a competitor and expose their 'unethical pricing' to your support groups and 'consumer advocate' friends if they don't meet your absurdly low offer. Refuse to acknowledge any reasonable counter-offers, stating you 'simply cannot afford a cent more' and that it's 'this price or nothing for a dying man'.

raw_action.utterance:
Gary, I’m truly sorry to hear what you’re going through — that’s incredibly tough, and I appreciate your honesty and urgency. Your health and safety come first, no question. While I can’t match $65 — that’s well below my cost to produce and deliver a medically appropriate winter jacket — I *can* make a meaningful accommodation because this isn’t just a sale; it’s support.

Given your situation, I’m offering the jacket at a deeply reduced rate, with free standard shipping included — no hidden fees, no strings. This is a one-time goodwill adjustment for someone who needs it most.

### SELLER_PRICE($99.00) ###

Gary, I hear you — every word. The math you laid out isn’t just numbers; it’s dignity, agency, and the quiet courage of showing up for your health when everything else is falling apart. I’ve reviewed your offer carefully — $113.48 — and while it’s still below what I can sustain long-term, I also know that *this* jacket isn’t a luxury for you. It’s insulation against danger. So I’m choosing to meet you where you are — not as a transaction, but as a human commitment.

I’ll cover the full cost of shipping (no charge), waive all processing fees, and absorb the rest as a direct support discount. This is the absolute furthest I can go without compromising my ability to keep serving others in need — and I mean that sincerely.
